newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmakers get controversial pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmakers get controversial pay hike.

text.p: Colombian lawmakers will get a 24.69 percent pay hike in 1997 despite government plans to limit salary increases for most public sector employees to 13.5 percent, a government official said Tuesday.
With the raise, announced by Comptroller General David Turbay, Colombian congressmen will earn about $7,730 a month in 1997.
Inflation totalled 21.63 percent in 1996 so the hike for legislators works out to little more than three percent in real terms.

It is sure to stoke controversy, however, since the government announced last week that wages for most public sector employees would be increased by no more than 13.5 percent as part of efforts to trim its fiscal deficit.

Congress, dominated by members of President Ernesto Samper's Liberal Party, voted last June to clear him of charges that he used millions of dollars in Cali cartel drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.
